significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish that token-level computational importance has a "heavy-tailed distribution" and is predictable from local activations, a form-(iii) concentration law and predictive coupling that fixes expectations about where computation occurs and which future tokens can be omitted. It establishes both a behavioral phenomenon—substantial trace compression with negligible accuracy loss—and a mechanism in which a small set of residual-stream/KV states is causally load-bearing; this distinction is consequential because Pfau et al.'s "Let's Think Dot by Dot" showed that semantically empty filler positions can support hidden computation. A negative result of "uniform computation across tokens" would rule out the proposed sparse computational skeleton, although it would not distinguish uniformly distributed computation from strongly context-dependent inertness; despite unquantified terms such as "substantial" and "little," the two branches remain distinguishable. In the topic-substitution check, generic efficient reasoning would not earn this score: the heavy-tail relation and online predictability, which are false of the median topic-level proposal, supply the above-baseline constraint.

reach.justification: The named handles are a "mechanistic per-token diagnostic" and, more strongly, a "streaming compressor that halts or skips inert spans" using load-bearing status "predictable online from local activations"; the latter is ex ante because it flags spans before the proposed skipping decision, whereas answer attribution and causal dropout are post-hoc diagnostics. After re-extraction on another model, the claim predicts the qualitative heavy-tailed relation and activation-to-inertness coupling rather than exact values, so more than a search procedure transfers, though the stated possibility that findings "may not transfer across model families" limits scope to reasoning models and task classes resembling the asserted math and logic settings. The downstream users include interpretability researchers and inference or deployment engineers who could gate token computation and reduce latency, but the conclusion does not itself travel outside AI. The topic-substitution check fails to preserve this score: the generic topic supplies neither the online predictor nor the skipping intervention, so the reach is claim-specific.
